problem: The text says total order has 'two common implementations' but only the sequencer is described. The second one is never named, so a student looks for something that is not there and may think a replicated sequencer is the only alternative.
fix: Name both: (1) sequencer — one process stamps each message 1, 2, 3 …, members deliver in that order; (2) agreement-based (symmetric) total order — members attach Lamport timestamps and break ties by process id, or agree on a sequence number among themselves. Then say that a replicated sequencer is a special case of the second.

problem: 'members run an agreement round to choose the next number' is muddled. Consensus is used to agree on the ordering of messages, or to choose a new sequencer after a failure, not to pick the next sequence number for each message.
fix: Write: 'If the sequencer is a bottleneck or failure point, the group can run agreement to order messages or to elect a new sequencer; that agreement is consensus, left to Unit 5.'

problem: The figure shows m2 going only from P2 to P3. Group communication sends every message to every member, and m2's vector (1,1,0) was built after P2 delivered m1. As drawn, a student may think causal order is defined over ordinary point-to-point messages between selected pairs.
fix: Show m2 as sent to P1 and P3 (P1's copy can be omitted with a note 'm2 also sent to P1'), and state once that every message in the example is multicast to all three members.
